legend: Olya has got a directed non-weighted graph, consisting of n vertexes and m edges. We will consider that the graph vertexes are indexed from 1 to n in some manner. Then for any graph edge that goes from vertex v to vertex u the following inequation holds: v < u.
Now Olya wonders, how many ways there are to add an arbitrary (possibly zero) number of edges to the graph so as the following conditions were met:
You can reach vertexes number i + 1, i + 2, ..., n from any vertex number i (i < n).
For any graph edge going from vertex v to vertex u the following inequation fulfills: v < u.
There is at most one edge between any two vertexes.
The shortest distance between the pair of vertexes i, j (i < j), for which j - i ≤ k holds, equals j - i edges.
The shortest distance between the pair of vertexes i, j (i < j), for which j - i > k holds, equals either j - i or j - i - k edges.
We will consider two ways distinct, if there is the pair of vertexes i, j (i < j), such that first resulting graph has an edge from i to j and the second one doesn't have it.
Help Olya. As the required number of ways can be rather large, print it modulo 1000000007 (109 + 7).
input: The first line contains three space-separated integers n, m, k (2 ≤ n ≤ 106, 0 ≤ m ≤ 105, 1 ≤ k ≤ 106).

The next m lines contain the description of the edges of the initial graph. The i-th line contains a pair of space-separated integers ui, vi (1 ≤ ui < vi ≤ n) — the numbers of vertexes that have a directed edge from ui to vi between them.

It is guaranteed that any pair of vertexes ui, vi has at most one edge between them. It also is guaranteed that the graph edges are given in the order of non-decreasing ui. If there are multiple edges going from vertex ui, then it is guaranteed that these edges are given in the order of increasing vi.
output: Print a single integer — the answer to the problem modulo 1000000007 (109 + 7).
note: In the first sample there are two ways: the first way is not to add anything, the second way is to add a single edge from vertex 2 to vertex 5.

legend.ai: Olya 有一个有向无带权图，包含 n 个顶点和 m 条边。我们假设图的顶点按某种方式从 1 到 n 编号。那么对于任意一条从顶点 v 到顶点 u 的图边，以下不等式成立：v < u。
现在 Olya 想知道，有多少种方式可以向图中添加任意（可能为零）数量的边，使得满足以下条件：
从任意编号为 i 的顶点（i < n）可以到达编号为 i + 1, i + 2, ..., n 的顶点。
对于任意一条从顶点 v 到顶点 u 的图边，以下不等式成立：v < u。
任意两个顶点之间至多有一条边。
对于满足 j - i ≤ k 的顶点对 i, j（i < j），它们之间的最短距离等于 j - i 条边。
对于满足 j-i>k 的顶点对 i、j（i<j），它们之间的最短距离等于 j-i 条边或 j-i-k 条边。
如果存在顶点对 i、j（i<j），使得第一个得到的图中有一条从 i 到 j 的边，而第二个图中没有这条边，则认为这两种方案不同。
帮助 Olya。由于所求方案数可能非常大，请输出其对 1000000007（10^9+7）取模的结果。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中有两种方式：第一种是什么也不添加，第二种是从顶点 2 到顶点 5 添加一条边。

input.ai: 第一行包含三个以空格分隔的整数 n、m、k（2≤n≤10^6，0≤m≤10^5，1≤k≤10^6）。
接下来的 m 行描述初始图中的边。第 i 行包含一对以空格分隔的整数 ui、vi（1≤ui<vi≤n），表示一条从 ui 指向 vi 的有向边的两个顶点编号。
保证任意一对顶点 ui、vi 之间至多有一条边。还保证图中的边按照 ui 非递减的顺序给出。如果有多条边从顶点 ui 出发，则保证这些边按照 vi 递增的顺序给出。
